title: Minimax Experimental Design under Network Interference via Two-Hop Clique Packings
banked_reason: The all-procedure packing lower bound is general, but the two-sided minimax characterization is restricted to graphs admitting a supplied bounded-degree quotient partition with proportionally large squared-graph cliques; arbitrary graphs remain uncharacterized.
gap_reasons: The all-procedure packing lower bound is general, but the two-sided minimax characterization is restricted to graphs admitting a supplied bounded-degree quotient partition with proportionally large squared-graph cliques; arbitrary graphs remain uncharacterized.
The degree-factor novelty comparison applies only to the two explicit Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje lower expressions, not to their implicit conflict-graph characterization.
The sharp Theta(1/k) rate is established on constructed projective-plane block and chain families, while the planning result is only an MSE screen rather than an inference or power theorem.

proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an arbitrary-design clique-packing lower certificate, a matching cluster-exposure upper bound under a supplied bounded-quotient partition, and sharp rates on disconnected and connected projective-plane incidence families. After bounded cleanup, the math and decision panels passed with no findings and the cited source was attested. The general referee still graded the delivered scope subfield, below the field floor; arbitrary-graph matching, an optimization algorithm, and nonconstructed-network validation remain open.
tldr: A single assignment cannot reveal both endpoint signs carried by any two-hop clique. Tensorizing that observation over disjoint cliques and optimizing the sign amplitudes under a global endpoint \(q\)-moment budget yields an explicit all-design, all-estimator minimax MSE certificate. For both the combined budget and the exact published separate-arm budget, independent cluster coins and a Horvitz--Thompson endpoint estimator match the certificate, up to constants, whenever a partition has bounded quotient degree and contains proportionally large two-hop cliques. Projective-plane incidence blocks and bridge-connected chains have risk \(\Theta(1/k)=\Theta(d^2/n)\) under both conventions despite codegree one, with \(k=d\) giving \(\Theta(n^{-1/3})\). The graph certificate is a necessary precision diagnostic for full-rollout trial planning; no synthetic incidence graph is claimed to model an observed trial.
gap: Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje characterize the minimax problem through a conflict graph, but their explicit GATE lower functionals can remain a degree factor below their spectral upper bound. Existing graph-cluster designs provide estimators without a matching all-procedure converse.
fill: The project derives the optimized packing certificate, proves its exact normalization under combined and separate-arm endpoint budgets, supplies a bounded-quotient attaining estimator, and uses connected incidence chains to show a sharp low-codegree rate that strictly strengthens the published explicit lower bounds.
